task_description: Create a new userspace tool tools/muntutils/ implemented in BOTH C and C++ with two capabilities: (1) a SAFE-BY-DEFAULT source trimmer that determines statically (and best-effort dynamically) which functions are actually reachable across the source tree and emits a slimmed representation into a SEPARATE output tree, only rewriting originals in place behind an explicit opt-in flag that first creates a backup; and (2) size/stats reporting that measures raw source, slimmed source, and compiled artifacts and generates a dual-audience report (plain-language summary for an ordinary adult user plus detailed numbers for a programmer). Follow the repo's per-tool conventions exactly (build.sh, install.sh, README.md, .hss, .hsss, 1-2-3-4.mmd modeled on tools/size and tools/limit), carry the exact NCSU attribution 'Program based on Science at NCSU - Max Rupplin - MEARVK LLC 2026.', and integrate into the tools build chain without breaking pcopy/pmove.

verification.summary: build.sh builds the C+C++ program with the system gcc/g++ 11.5.0 fallback (derived GCC 16.2.0 not present) and prints the expected 'does not advertise -fme-metadata' warning; exit 0. `make -C tools muntutils` compiles all three TUs from a clean state and links via the Makefile chain (exit 0); the dependency-free muntutils target builds despite the PRE-EXISTING, out-of-scope pcopy.c bug (line 62 0xPC) that breaks the aggregate `all` target. `make -C tools clean` cleans muntutils too. Runtime (the project has no test harness; validation is compile + run per repo convention): default `trim <src> --out <dir>` leaves originals byte-identical (sha256sum -c OK) and writes a slim tree to the separate out dir with confidently-dead static functions removed while keeping used/main/non-static functions (conservative); `--in-place` creates a .bak backup per rewritten file and refuses in-place without the explicit flag; `--strict` additionally trims unreferenced non-static functions; `report --slim <dir> --out <file>` emits markdown with raw source stats, slim source stats, compiled-artifact stats, a plain-language 'Summary for everyone', and a 'Details for a programmer' section; `--version` prints muntutils 1.00. test_quality: repo has no unit-test framework (size/limit ship none); the runtime checks genuinely exercise the trimmer and reporter code paths (they would fail if the logic were reverted), so verification is meaningful rather than static assertions. docker_build skipped: no Dockerfile for this tool and network is restricted. Committed on branch feat/muntutils-source-trimmer-sizer (5cb9aaebfa); not pushed. Known cosmetic limitation (documented, out of scope): for very small dead functions the stub comment can make slim source marginally larger than raw, and the report clamps the shrink percentage to 0.0 in that case. REVIEW FIX ITERATION 1 (addresses 2026-09-01-005900-review.md NEEDS_CHANGES): (issue 1) muntutils_trim.cpp now collects every identifier-shaped token inside any string literal (new collect_quoted_identifiers pass) and promotes any that matches a defined function name to a conservative root, closing the general name-based-dispatch hole beyond dlsym/GetProcAddress; the reproduction case (my_register("live_via_custom_loader")) now KEEPS the function (0 dead) instead of stubbing it. (issue 2) when a removal is proposed while any string literal matches a defined function name, an unresolved note is emitted and confidence is capped at 90% so it no longer reads 100% in that blind spot (verified: dead fn + string-name match reports 90%). (issue 3) run_trim now rejects an --out that resolves inside (or equals) the source tree via realpath-based containment check, preventing re-scan of generated slim output; a shared-prefix sibling like src_slim is still allowed. (issue 4, out-of-scope pcopy) documented in README.md that `make -C tools muntutils` is the intended entry point and that aggregate all/install are expected to fail until the unrelated pcopy 0xPC fix lands; pcopy/pmove NOT modified. All TUs still compile clean under gcc/g++ -std=c11/c++17 -Wall -Wextra -Werror -O2; build.sh and clean `make -C tools muntutils` both exit 0; safe-by-default and .bak backup contracts re-verified.
